title: Can you give your own example for every rule?
description: One own example is made for each of the five rules of adding and the five rules of subtracting, and each is checked by sending the lift between floors. The video breaks the slip of thinking that the sign of the first number written decides the answer.
teaching_notes: One idea: any example is good if the lift ends where the rule says. Watch for students who keep the sign of the first number written, for instance in negative plus positive.

video_script.why: The child makes a fresh example for each of the ten rules and checks it by moving a lift between floors.
video_script.substitution: Choose two small numbers, treat the first as the starting floor and the second as the movement, and read the floor where the lift stops.
video_script.anchor: the lift of the book beside its floors, from below the ground to above it
video_script.payoff_line: Every example ends on the floor its rule promises

final_answer.value: Open-ended: own example for each of the 5 addition rules and 5 subtraction rules, each checked in the lift
final_answer.spoken: one example of our own for each of the ten rules, each checked in the lift

names.{{NAME_8}}: the Indian mathematician who gave rules for adding and subtracting positive numbers, negative numbers and zero in 628 CE

hold_back: Answer: ten examples, each checked in the lift
never_show: the claim that the sign of the first number always wins
maths_rules: addition rule 1: 4 + 3 = 7; start on floor 4, go up 3, reach floor 7
addition rule 2: (−4) + (−6) = −10; add the sizes 4 + 6 = 10 and keep the minus
addition rule 3: 7 + (−9) = −2; the greater size is 9, 9 − 7 = 2, and the sign of the greater is minus
slip test: (−4) + 9 = 5; the sign of the first number does not decide
subtraction rule 1: 9 − 4 = 5, the movement from floor 4 up to floor 9
subtraction rule 2: 4 − 9 = −5, the movement from floor 9 down to floor 4
video_script.design: One lift shaft with floors from −10 to 10. Each own example is shown as the lift starting on a floor and moving, with arrows in teal for up and amber for down.

narration: <bookmark mark='book'/>This is a question from your book about the rules of {{NAME_8}}.
<bookmark mark='cards'/>We must give our own example for each of the five adding rules and the five subtracting rules.
<bookmark mark='lift'/>The lift can tell us if an example is right.
<bookmark mark='ask'/>Can we make an example for every rule and be sure it works?

<bookmark mark='sub'/>The target floor minus the starting floor gives the movement.
<bookmark mark='dir'/>A positive press goes up, and a negative press goes down.
<bookmark mark='test'/>If the lift stops where the rule says, the example is good.

beats.on_screen: adding rule 1: 4 + 3 = 7; adding rule 2: (−4) + (−6) = −10, add the sizes 4 + 6 = 10 and keep the minus

marks.r1: the lift starts on floor 4 and the press 3 is chosen
marks.up: the lift goes up 3 floors and 7 appears on the target floor
marks.r2: the lift starts on floor −4 and the press −6 is chosen
marks.down: the lift goes down 6 floors and −10 appears on the target floor
marks.keep: the sizes 4 and 6 are added and the minus sign is kept

beats.moves_through: the lift goes up three floors, then down six floors
narration: <bookmark mark='r1'/>Step one, two positives, four and three.
<bookmark mark='up'/>The lift starts on floor four and goes up three floors to floor seven.
<bookmark mark='r2'/>Next, two negatives, minus four and minus six.
<bookmark mark='down'/>The lift starts on floor minus four and goes down six floors to minus ten.
<bookmark mark='keep'/>Four and six make ten, and the minus sign stays.

beats.on_screen: different signs: 7 + (−9) = −2; the greater size is 9, 9 − 7 = 2, the sign of the greater is minus; also (−4) + 9 = 5

marks.r3: the lift starts on floor 7 and the press −9 is chosen
marks.end: the lift goes down 9 floors and stops on floor −2
marks.rule: the greater size 9 is circled and 9 − 7 = 2 is written with a minus sign
marks.slip: (−4) + 9 = 5 is written and the lift stops above the ground

beats.removed: the examples of adding rules 1 and 2
beats.moves_through: the lift goes down from floor 7 to floor −2
narration: <bookmark mark='r3'/>Step two, a positive and a negative, seven and minus nine.
<bookmark mark='end'/>The lift starts on floor seven and goes down nine floors to floor minus two.
<bookmark mark='rule'/>The greater size is nine, and nine take away seven is two.
The sign of the greater is minus.
<bookmark mark='slip'/>Minus four plus nine ends on floor five, so the first sign does not decide.

beats.on_screen: adding rule 4: 6 + (−6) = 0, up 6 and down 6 bring the lift back; adding rule 5: (−7) + 0 = −7, a movement of 0 keeps the lift where it is

marks.r4: the lift goes down 6 floors from floor 6 to the ground floor
marks.r5: the lift stays on floor −7 and (−7) + 0 = −7 is written

beats.moves_through: the lift goes down six floors to the ground floor
narration: <bookmark mark='r4'/>Step three, start on floor six and press minus six.
<bookmark mark='r4b'/>The lift comes down to the ground, so six plus minus six is zero.
<bookmark mark='r5'/>Pressing nothing is a movement of zero, so minus seven plus zero stays minus seven.

beats.on_screen: subtraction rule 1: 9 − 4 = 5, from floor 4 up to floor 9; subtraction rule 2: 4 − 9 = −5, from floor 9 down to floor 4

marks.s1: the rule Target Floor − Starting Floor = Movement is written again
marks.ex1: an arrow goes from floor 4 up to floor 9 and 9 − 4 = 5 is written
marks.ex2: an arrow goes from floor 9 down to floor 4 and 4 − 9 = −5 is written

beats.moves_through: the lift goes up from floor 4 to floor 9, then down again
narration: <bookmark mark='s1'/>Step four, subtraction is the movement from the second floor to the first.
<bookmark mark='ex1'/>Nine take away four moves the lift from floor four up to floor nine.
That is plus five.
<bookmark mark='ex2'/>Four take away nine moves the lift from floor nine down to floor four.
That is minus five.

beats.on_screen: subtraction rule 3: 6 − (−5) = 11, the same as 6 + 5; rule 4: 8 − 8 = 0; rule 5: (−6) − 0 = −6 and 0 − (−6) = 6

marks.s3: an arrow goes from floor −5 up to floor 6 and 6 − (−5) = 11 is written
marks.s4: the lift stays on the same floor and 8 − 8 = 0 is written
marks.s5: (−6) − 0 = −6 is written, then an arrow goes from floor −6 up to floor 0 and 0 − (−6) = 6 is written

beats.moves_through: the lift goes up from floor −5 to floor 6, then from floor −6 to floor 0
narration: <bookmark mark='s3'/>Step five, take away a negative number.
Six take away minus five moves the lift from floor minus five up to floor six.
<bookmark mark='same'/>That is eleven floors up, the same as six plus five.
<bookmark mark='s4'/>Eight take away eight needs no movement, so the answer is zero.
<bookmark mark='s5'/>Minus six take away zero stays minus six.
Zero take away minus six moves the lift from floor minus six up to floor zero.
That is six floors.

marks.check: the rule Starting Floor + Movement = Target Floor is written

narration: <bookmark mark='check'/>Step six, check by adding each movement back to its starting floor.
<bookmark mark='c1'/>Minus five plus eleven lands on floor six, which matches.
<bookmark mark='c2'/>Four plus five lands on floor nine, which matches too.
